title: CSS: Animations and Transitions
text:
CSS can create animations and smooth transitions using the keyframes property.

To create an animation or transition, we need to start calling the keyframes property like this:

@keyframes thisisananimation { }

As shown above, we will call @keyframes followed by the desired name of your animation.

Now, we must fill out our animation. Leaving nothing in the curly brackets makes the animation pretty dull. So dull, in fact, that it will do nothing! Let's fix that now.

To fix this problem, we'll need to add a couple percentages. These are here to show that show ___ into the animation, ___ will happen.

Here's how we'll set this up.

@keyframes thisisananimation { 

   0% {
       /**Here, put what you want the properties that are changing in the animation or transition to start out as.**/
   }
   100% {
       /**Here, put what you want the properties that are changing in the animation or transition to end as.**/
   }

}
